title: H2 Essay Questions by Topic
doc: 2f H2 Essay Questions by Topic v0.13.docx

sections.title: 1. What this doc is and how it was built
bullets: All H2 essay questions (20 marks each): Paper 1 Q3–Q6 (Clusters 1 and 2) and Paper 2 Q3–Q4 (Cluster 3). That is 282 essays from 47 school-years (43 pages). No essay uses a diagram.

Grouped by cluster, then by syllabus sub-topic, then by school and year. Largest groups: 3.1.3 Liveable Cities (27), 3.2.3 Responses to Climate Change (27), 1.1.3 Managing Resources (26), 2.1.3 Floods in the Humid Tropics (26), 1.2.3 Relative Influence of Actors (24). Smallest: 3.1.1 Sustainable Urban Development (2), 2.1.2 Drainage Basin Hydrology (5), 1.2.1 Development (6).
Under each question heading, a 'Syllabus' line gives the key question it tests (as in doc 1).

Question wording is typed from each school's question paper. Every essay was checked: 20 marks, and the wording matches the verbatim wording in the reading notes (279 match exactly; 3 differ only because the notes paraphrase).

sections.title: 2. Assumptions
bullets: An essay is filed under the sub-topic of its key question. 34 essays have two key questions; they are filed under the first. Section 3 lists the 14 whose two key questions are in different sub-topics.
Within a sub-topic, essays are listed by school and year, not by key question (see section 4).
The section line is standardised: 'Section B — Cluster 1' (P1 Q3–Q4), 'Section B — Cluster 2' (P1 Q5–Q6) and 'Section C — Cluster 3' (P2 Q3–Q4). This matches every school's paper.
Wording is kept exactly as printed, including slips in the paper (e.g. YIJC 2026 P2 Q3 has no opening quotation mark).
Word files were converted to PDF with LibreOffice before extracting text, so line breaks can differ slightly from the printed paper.

sections.title: 4. To consider
bullets: List essays within each sub-topic by key question instead of by school (e.g. all flood-management essays together under 2.1.3). This makes it easy to compare how different schools phrase the same question.
Add a one-page index: key question → schools and years that set an essay on it, so gaps in coverage are easy to see (e.g. only 2 essays on 3.1.1 Sustainable Urban Development).
Combine with doc 2c (H1 essays) for the topics both levels share (H1 Cluster 1 = H2 Cluster 3).
